The Figure 3 example compares LGPE-SRTM with lp-ntPET under transient
(gamma) and sustained (logistic) activation. Each simulation has 50
subjects and a group activation amplitude of 0.05. Because the data
are simulated, the estimated curves can be compared with the truth.

## Simulate and fit

The simulation returns the observed time–activity curves in `df`, the
latent trajectories in `truth`.
To fit your own data, supply one row per subject and frame (long format) with columns
`id`, `time` (minutes from scan start), `ct` (target TAC), `cr`
(reference TAC), and `onset_time` (minutes from scan start, constant
within subject). This example also uses a numeric `group` column coded
0 for control and 1 for activation. The following code shows the gamma case. 

```{r fit, eval=FALSE}
library(lgpesrtm)

sim <- simulate_lgpe_pet(
  n = 50, activation_amplitude = 0.05,
  activation_shape = "gamma", seed = 20260566
)

df <- sim$df

fit <- fit_lgpe_srtm(
  df = df,
  predvars = list(k2a = "group")
)

fit$k2a[[1]]              # Fitted curve for the first subject
fit$beta_k2a_mat[, 2]     # Activation-minus-control curve
```

## Change fitting settings

Pass only the settings you want to change. This example turns on
iteration plots while keeping the default tolerance of `1e-4` and
iteration limit of `1000`.

```{r control, eval=FALSE}
fit_with_plots <- fit_lgpe_srtm(
  df = df,
  predvars = list(k2a = "group"),
  control = list(plot_iterations = TRUE)
)
```

The default fit shares a fixed-effect GP amplitude across the
`k2a` terms. The default kernel length scale is 10 minutes and the
starting value for the noise variance proportionality factor is 10.
You can override entries in `par_in`, for example with
`par_in = list(theta1 = 8)` to use an 8-minute length scale.

## Reproduce the plots

The installed script runs both simulations and fits LGPE-SRTM once per
scenario and lp-ntPET separately for each subject. The subject panels
show individual curves and group summaries. The contrast panels show
the estimated activation-minus-control curves and pointwise intervals
computed as estimate ± 1.96 standard errors.

```{r figure_ex, eval=FALSE}
example <- new.env()
sys.source(system.file("reproduce", "figure_ex.R", package = "lgpesrtm",
                       mustWork = TRUE), envir = example)
print(example$p_k2a)
print(example$p_activation_beta)
```

The fitting chunks are evaluated on demand so building the vignette
does not rerun the simulations.
